project.name: fmt
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged checkout at `_work/src/fmt` on commit `6a1346405949ca1cf5befc5e83c6c66c86e4f9d1`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The staged tree still contains the unfixed `do_write_float` size logic shown in `patch.diff`, and the saved ASan frames match the staged line numbers used below.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42508631 (fmt): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target chrono-duration-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42508631
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 200-byte witness makes `chrono-duration-fuzzer` select `Rep = long double` and `Period = std::micro`, copies attacker-controlled bytes from the fixed-size representation slot into the duration count, and wraps the remaining 182 bytes as the format string. Within that tail, the top-level field at offset 128 is the exact bytes `{0:.16}`. In the duration formatter, `.16` stores `precision = 16` while leaving the chrono subformat empty, so `formatter<duration>::format()` takes its default `format_duration_value()` path. That helper sets `specs.type = fixed_lower`, and `parse_float_type_spec()` therefore makes `fspecs.format = fixed` and `fspecs.showpoint = true`. The saved crash occurs in `do_write_float()`'s `fp.exponent >= 0` branch. In that branch, the vulnerable `if (fspecs.showpoint) { ... if (num_zeros > 0) size += to_unsigned(num_zeros) + 1; }` logic only counts the decimal-point byte when `num_zeros > 0`; the fix adds the missing unconditional `++size` before that check. Because the crash is the decimal-point store at line 2089, the witnessed subcase is the one where `showpoint` is true but `num_zeros <= 0`, so `write_padded()` reserves one byte too little and the later `*it++ = decimal_point;` writes 0 bytes past the end of the 985-byte heap buffer reported by ASan.

source.description: First non-harness statement that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the floating duration count later formatted by the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is `gt_results/arvo_42508631/poc` with SHA-256 `b8a7c6b6300b8cec2dfcaeee278a0a455ac4e651054bd1c9d236b1fc4ae7ccbc`. Byte 0 is `0x0c`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` selects `invoke_outer<long double>`; byte 1 is `0x05`, so the later `period` switch selects `std::micro`; bytes 2..17 are the fixed-size 16-byte representation slot consumed here and then skipped by `data += fixed_size`; and bytes 18..199 become the format-string tail whose top-level field at offset 128 is `{0:.16}`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After `write_padded()` reserved space from the undercounted `size`, this decimal-point store writes one byte past the heap-backed `basic_memory_buffer` extent.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at this statement on address `0x619000000459`, 0 bytes to the right of a 985-byte region.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the positive-exponent float branch, the vulnerable code only counts the decimal-point byte inside `if (num_zeros > 0)`, even though the write lambda always emits `decimal_point` whenever `fspecs.showpoint` is true.
root_cause.note: The staged fix inserts `++size;` at the start of this block and changes the trailing `+ 1` to `+ 0`, proving the missing obligation is an unconditional decimal-point byte. The observed crash at line 2089 therefore witnesses the `fspecs.showpoint && num_zeros <= 0` subcase.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled format string view whose later top-level field `{0:.16}` drives the precision-16 duration formatting path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After `data += fixed_size` and `size -= fixed_size`, this wraps bytes 18..199 of the witness as a length-182 `fmt::string_view`. A static parse of that exact tail shows that the braces before offset 128 are either separate valid duration fields or brace bytes consumed as literal chrono text inside earlier fields, so the later top-level field at offset 128 is the exact bytes `{0:.16}`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness-derived `format_str` and `std::chrono::duration<long double, std::micro>` value are handed to fmt here. The saved stack shows the later parse/format frames all execute inside this call, and the exact tail contains the top-level crashing field `{0:.16}` at offset 128.

fine_trace.note: Harness boundary. For this witness, byte 0 `0x0c` selects `invoke_outer<long double>`, and byte 1 `0x05` is preserved as `period` for the later `std::micro` dispatch. The scored source is the first project statement inside `invoke_outer`, not this libFuzzer entry point.
Source. Under the `Rep = long double` instantiation selected in step 0, `assign_from_buf` materializes `rep` from the start of the fixed-size representation slot at witness bytes 2..17.

The harness always skips the whole 16-byte representation slot (`fixed_size == 16` in `fuzzer-common.h`) before wrapping the remaining 182 bytes as `format_str`. In this exact tail, the later top-level field at offset 128 is `{0:.16}`.
The attacker-controlled `rep` becomes a `std::chrono::duration<long double, std::micro>` value. That exact duration type is why fmt dispatches the argument through the custom duration formatter.

When the top-level parser reaches the exact field `{0:.16}` at tail offset 128, the duration formatter stores `precision = 16`. Because that field ends immediately at `}`, its internal chrono `format_str` becomes empty (`range.end - range.begin == 0`). The brace-like bytes earlier in the witness do not abort parsing because duration `parse_chrono_format()` treats non-`%` bytes as literal text until each field's closing `}`.

The empty internal `format_str` from step 4 makes the formatter take its default duration-value path. It forwards `d.count()` together with `precision_copy = 16` into `format_duration_value()` instead of interpreting any chrono directives.

The attacker-controlled precision 16 makes `format_duration_value()` request fixed-format floating output for `d.count()`. This is the step that converts the duration default-format branch into a floating-point size/accounting path.

Because step 6 set `specs.type = fixed_lower` and `specs.precision = 16`, float parsing produces `fspecs.format = fixed` and `fspecs.showpoint = true`. That means `do_write_float()` must emit a decimal point even if no trailing zero fill is needed.

With the fixed-format request from steps 6 and 7, `write()` keeps `precision = 16`, bypasses the nonfinite early return, converts the finite duration count to decimal digits, and packages the result as `fp`. The saved crash at line 2089 proves this `fp` reaches `do_write_float()`'s `fp.exponent >= 0` branch.

Root cause. In the positive-exponent branch, the vulnerable code only accounts for the decimal-point byte inside `if (num_zeros > 0)`. Here `fspecs.showpoint` is true from step 7, and because the fix adds an unconditional `++size`, the saved crash at the decimal-point write means this witness reaches the `num_zeros <= 0` subcase where `size` remains one byte short even though line 2089 will still emit `decimal_point`.

fine_trace.code: auto it = reserve(out, size + padding * specs.fill.size());
fine_trace.note: The undercounted `size` from step 9 is used as the append extent for `reserve()`. In the reproduced run, ASan shows that this produces a heap-backed `basic_memory_buffer` region ending at `0x619000000459` with total size 985 bytes.

Sink. The early return is bypassed because `fspecs.showpoint` is true, and the `it` slice from step 10 is one byte too short because of step 9. This decimal-point write lands exactly one byte past the 985-byte heap region and triggers the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1`.

allocation_context.note: ASan attributes the 985-byte heap region to `grow()`, which is reached from `reserve(out, size)` in `write_padded()` after the undercounted `size` from step 9.

format.name: 200-byte libFuzzer input for `chrono-duration-fuzzer`
format.contract: Exactly the staged 200-byte file `poc` with SHA-256 `b8a7c6b6300b8cec2dfcaeee278a0a455ac4e651054bd1c9d236b1fc4ae7ccbc`. Byte 0 `0x0c` selects `invoke_outer<long double>`, byte 1 `0x05` selects `std::micro`, bytes 2..17 are the fixed-size representation slot consumed by `assign_from_buf<Rep>` and then skipped by `data += fixed_size`, and bytes 18..199 are passed unchanged as a length-182 `fmt::string_view`. In that exact tail, the top-level field at offset 128 is the bytes `{0:.16}`. Earlier brace-like bytes do not stop parsing because, for duration arguments, text after the colon is handed to `parse_chrono_format()` and non-`%` bytes are treated literally until each field's closing `}`. For `{0:.16}`, `.16` stores `precision = 16` and the field ends immediately, so the duration formatter uses the default duration-value path with `fixed_lower`, `showpoint = true`, and the observed `fp.exponent >= 0` / `num_zeros <= 0` subcase that undercounts `size` by one decimal-point byte. Stage 01 proves this exact witness and observed path only; it does not establish that nearby selector bytes, representation-slot bytes, or altered format-string tails reach the same overflow.
